name: Pipework Bank
desc: A bank of industrial process pipes running across the mid-ground on hanger rods — bolted flanges, welded seams, jacketed lagging and corrosion bloom — while a raking work-light drifts along the crowns of the tubes, a mast shadow crosses the run, steam sighs from a relief valve and condensate drips off the low line.

scale.doc: depth of the pipe band vs frame — pipe diameter scales with it

density.doc: how many parallel runs (3-8) plus fittings, grain and steam

decay.doc: corrosion bloom, drip staining and grime worked into the runs

speed.doc: rate of the light sweep, steam and drips

hue.doc: steel hue (206 = cold plant grey; rust always answers on the complement)

x.doc: anchor x — the light and the mast shadow orbit this point

y.doc: centre line of the bank as a canvas fraction

alpha.doc: opacity of the lighting pass — drop it to sit the bank back in the haze

style.doc: steel: painted plant steel, modelled cylindrical light and hard speculars · lagged: aluminium-jacketed insulation — chalky matte cladding, seam bands and pop rivets, no gloss · oxide: abandoned and corroded, dark key, flaking iron and deep drip staining · schematic: a P&ID, not an object — no mass at all, double-line headers with valve bowties, tag bubbles and dashed instrument runs, and a signal pulse walking each line · xray: weld-inspection radiograph — negative greyscale, dark bore, walls bright at the tangents, bead absorption bands across every joint

act.doc: drift: the plant idles, the light wanders · purge: the relief valves surge on every kick · cold: shut down — the light barely moves, nothing vents

seed.doc: deterministic seed for run layout, fitting placement and corrosion
